# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect which has been a huge worry for the family, and they are working closely with the cardiologist to monitor and manage it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble with feeding as a baby, including latching on and spitting up, but this has mostly resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, and managing her seizures has been a challenge. They are trying different medications and therapies to find what works best for her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, which may affect her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away, such as the board in her classroom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip very easily, even with careful brushing and dental care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to keep up with her schoolwork due to her vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced speech delays as a younger child, but therapy has helped a lot with that.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and may have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia, and the family has had to take extra precautions to ensure it doesn't cause long-term issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further problems
* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing is not affected by the fluid in her ear
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and provide any necessary corrections or treatments
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's septal defect and adjust treatment as necessary
* Neurological review to manage the patient's epilepsy and adjust medications or therapies as necessary
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue and shortness of breath during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac concerns that need evaluation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower weight gain compared to peers, initially raising concerns about potential nutritional deficiencies or absorption issues, but is being monitored closely after dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding, with a few needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are a significant concern and are being managed by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, although in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sensitive to background noise, which affects his mood and behavior, and tends to get overwhelmed and frustrated in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board during lessons, affecting his ability to follow instructions and participate fully in class.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak tooth enamel, making his teeth more susceptible to decay and sensitivity, and is working on improving his oral hygiene routine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, with careful brushing being very important and regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems affect his ability to follow instructions and participate fully in class, potentially impacting his learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans due to more significant learning difficulties.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's sensitivity to noise and vision problems contribute to his behavioral challenges, including irritability and frustration in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a slightly different gait pattern, which is being monitored to ensure it doesn't develop into a more serious orthopedic issue later on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number having hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address weak tooth enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess potential heart conditions.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioral challenges.
* Neurological management and monitoring of seizures.
* Consideration of skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for any orthopedic concerns.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated in noisy places and rubs his eyes frequently when trying to focus.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had significant difficulties with feeding in infancy, which have since resolved.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids his age, possibly related to his overall development or balance, and has developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient frequently asks for repetitions because he didn't quite catch what was said the first time, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on objects or people, indicating potential vision problems.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone age and detect any skeletal anomalies.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired after playing for a bit, suggesting potential cardiac issues that lead to exhaustion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Mealtimes can be tough, and the patient has trouble eating sometimes, which affects his mood and energy levels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue that the doctors are keeping an eye on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: There's been fluid in the patient's ear for a while now, causing discomfort, and the patient has speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means his eyes get tired easily when looking at things closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods and drinks make the patient's teeth hurt due to sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech isn't as developed as expected for his age, and he doesn't talk as much as his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stands and walks a bit differently than other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stands and walks a bit differently than other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness.
* Regular hearing reviews to address the fluid in the ear and potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct hypermetropia.
* Consider a cardiac review to investigate potential heart conditions.
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess spinal and skeletal development.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and differences.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, requiring close management and prevention of seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear due to a buildup of fluid, requiring treatment with antibiotics.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes frequently, especially when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing, particularly with harder foods, and requires adaptations to make eating easier.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect and manage hearing loss

* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that is being closely monitored with regular appointments and tests.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and often refuses foods based on how they feel in her mouth, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting compared to other kids her age, and is working with therapists to help her catch up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid in her ear, which has affected her hearing somewhat, and is waiting for further assessment to see how it can be treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which is causing her some discomfort and blurred vision at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth, which is a concern for her smile and potential self-esteem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor spinal and bone development
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and catch-up
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Management of palatal abnormalities to support feeding and speech development

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular check-ups to monitor her heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky about food and refuses to eat certain things, which can make it challenging to ensure a balanced diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with a tethered cord, which may cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear a few months ago, which was treated with antibiotics, and she may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV and when reading books, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, even when eating hard foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient started talking later than her peers and may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers and speech has been a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delays, behavioral differences, and may have autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers and curved 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review to monitor heart health and detect any potential heart conditions
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to assess for spinal or hip abnormalities
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
